patch_description: Expert knowledge on the Heilbronn problem: for small n (n=11), the best known configurations (Goldberg-style) place most or all points on the boundary of the convex region — collinear triples on edges are avoided by using different spacings on each side, and boundary placement maximizes the "spread" that drives up the minimum triangle area. The current code only perturbs an interior lattice, which caps the achievable minimum area. I add a boundary-heavy deterministic seed generator (points distributed along the three edges with slightly different, golden-ratio-based spacings to avoid near-collinear triples), feed those seeds through the existing refine loop, and cut the seed budget from 30 to a smaller mixed set (10 lattice + 6 boundary) to keep eval_time low while focusing the search on the more promising boundary configurations.
